Evidence is scoped t
o the claim it supports: for a measured failure the span\nids, prompt indexes and reasons come from the first failed stage's row a

`model` takes
an id from the hosted catalog — `provider/name` form, e.g.\n`anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5` — and runs on your organization's credits
.\nProvider-native ids (e.g. `claude-sonnet-4-5`) are bring-your-own-key: pass\nthe key in `modelApiKeys`. A model the API can't e
xecute is rejected at\ncreate time with `VALIDATION_ERROR`; `details.hostedModels` lists the valid\nhosted ids for that provider.\
n\nReruns are even shorter: `{ \"suiteId\": \"...\" }` reruns the suite exactly as\nconfigured, connecting the suite's saved serve
r selection (the `202` response\nlists the resolved `servers`). Pass `serverIds` to override the selection; a\nsuite with no saved

selection requires it (`VALIDATION_ERROR` with
`details.reason: "NO_SAVED_SERVER_SELECTION"` otherwise).

### Running agains

t a project environment

A [project environment](#endpoints) is launchable only through a suite that has
it **attached**. Attac
h them first with\n`PATCH /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites/{suiteId}` and an `environmentIds`\narray (send `null` to detach them
all; `[]` is rejected — use `null`), then\npass `environmentId` on the run. It must be one of that suite's attached\nenvironments;
anything else is a `400` with\n`details.reason: \"ENVIRONMENT_NOT_ATTACHED\"`, raised before any case is\nauthored or any server

connected.

Omitting `environmentId` is meaningful, and depends on the suite:

* **no** attached environments → the run uses t
he saved server selection, as before;\n* **exactly one** attached → that environment is used automatically. The `202`\n response'
s `environment` field says so;\n* **several** attached → `400` with `details.reason: \"ENVIRONMENT_REQUIRED\"`,\n naming the cand

idates.

The environment supplies the closed server set — including the servers its
pinned plugin versions contribute — so `ser
verIds` is not required and is\n**rejected** alongside it (`400`), rather than accepted and ignored: honoring\nboth would connect
a different set than the run is stamped with. The same goes\nfor a `serverIds` override on an environment-based suite\n(`details.r

eason: "ENVIRONMENT_SERVERS_NOT_OVERRIDABLE"`).

The run is pinned to the environment revision resolved at launch: if the
env
ironment changes in between, the run is rejected with `CONFLICT` (409)\nrather than executing against a different configuration th

an the one whose
tools were captured. Use
`GET /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/resolve` to see what it
will
connect before launching.\n\nWhen creating a new inline suite, `POST .../eval-runs` also accepts `hosts: [{ host: \"Claude\", serv
ers: [\"my-server\"] }]`, using the same host name or ID and optional server selection as `POST .../eval-suites`. A single host is
selected for the run automatically. With multiple attachments, use `namedHostId` to select the run's client. For an existing suit
e, update its attachments first. If `hosts` is omitted, the backend supplies the project's default client.\n\nRun reads and listin
gs expose `client: { id, name, source, hostStyle?, modelId? }` when recorded. `id` is the named host ID or `null`; `source` is `en
vironment`, `attached_host`, `suite_default`, or `sdk`. The name is durable even if the host is deleted. SDK executions use `SDK h
arness`; `launcher.client` separately identifies the launching process. Older runs without a descriptor omit `client`. `modelSourc
e: \"case\"` means the run's sole model came from its case snapshot; `client_default` and `override` retain their existing meaning

s.

Every run records which environment it used. `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}` (and
the run listings) return `environment: { id,
name, revision }` — read from the\nrun's immutable snapshot, not the suite's current attachments — or `null` for a\nrun that used

a saved server selection.

Per-organization
concurrency is capped (default **2** concurrent runs); exceeding it returns
`429`

with `details.reason: "CONCURRENT_RUN_LIMIT"` — wait for an active run
to finish.

If a server answers `401 OAUTH_REQUIRED`,
complete the OAuth flow yourself\n(the SDK's `runOAuthLogin` handles interactive, headless, and\nclient-credentials flows) and upl
oad the token to one of the server's\n[accounts](#server-accounts). Subsequent runs inject the stored token, and\nrefresh it serve

r-side when you stored a refresh token.

## Reasoning effort

A reasoning effort is a **saved setting on a model selection**,
not a free-standing\nfield. A `ModelSelection` (`modelId`, `source`, an optional `connectionRef`, and a\n`fallback`) carries it as

`settings.reasoningEffort`, and the same shape is
accepted everywhere a model choice is saved:

| Where | Field |
| - | - |
| Client (`PATCH /projects/{projectId}/clients/{client}`) | `set.modelSelection` (or `config.modelSelection` on a whole-config rep
lacement) |\n| Project environment (`POST`, `PATCH`, `POST .../ensure-adhoc`) | `modelSelection`, read back on the environment |\n
| Eval case (`POST`, `PATCH .../cases`) | `models[].selection`, read back on the case |\n| Eval suite (`PATCH /projects/{projectId
}/eval-suites/{suiteId}`) | `executionConfig.modelSelection`, read back on the suite |\n\n```json theme={\"theme\":\"css-variables
`, `max`. Which of\n them a model accepts is `supportedReasoningEfforts` on each row of the public\n `GET /v1/models` catalog. A
n empty or absent list means no effort is offered for\n that model — do not guess one.\n* **Applied or refused, never dropped.**
A saved effort is applied by the route\n the run takes and recorded on the execution record, or refused with\n `capability_missi
ng` before any spend. An effort replaces the sampling\n temperature.\n* **A selection belongs to one model.** It must be for the
`model` / `modelId` it\n sits beside (`400` otherwise); sent alone it pins its own model. A bare model\n change on a suite or en
vironment drops a selection saved for the old model\n instead of failing.\n* **Cases keep their selections.** A `models` PATCH re
places the array, but an\n entry that omits `selection` keeps the case's existing selection for that\n model. Send `selection: n
ull` to drop it.\n* **Clearing.** `null` clears a saved selection on a client `set`, an environment\n or a suite, keeping the bar

e model id.
* **Never a secret.** A selection has no credential field; an unknown key
 (`apiKey`, …) is a `400`.
* **Environme
nts need the capability.** `GET .../environments/capabilities`\n reports `modelSelections`; an older deployment rejects the field
.\n* **`advancedConfig.reasoningEffort` is retired.** It was never applied, so\n writing it is a `400` pointing at `models[].sele

ction.settings`, and a stored
 value is refused by the runner.

`POST /chat-sessions/messages` takes a top-level `reasoningEff
ort` for a\nper-request effort. Like `temperature`, it is pinned on the session's **first\nturn** (a continuation that restates it

is refused), it wins over the effort a
`hostId`'s saved selection carries, and it cannot be combined with `temperature`.

The
SDK, CLI, MCP tools and in-app agent all go through the same operations:\n`--effort` / `reasoningEffort` is a shorthand that edits

the selection the target
already has, and is refused (`send modelSelection`) when there is none.
